name: Stockholm
tagline: A capital built on fourteen islands, with a medieval old town, royal palaces and great museums.
highlight: Wandering the cobbled lanes of Gamla Stan, then a waterside fika in the sun.
shortDescription: Sweden's elegant island capital: Gamla Stan, the Royal Palace, the Vasa Museum, Skansen, City Hall, design shops and an archipelago on its doorstep.
metaDescription: A Stockholm travel guide: Gamla Stan, the Vasa Museum, Royal Palace, Skansen, City Hall, ABBA Museum, Djurgarden, fika, where to stay and a three-day plan.

image.alt: The Royal Palace and Storkyrkan cathedral in Stockholm

intro: Stockholm is built across fourteen islands where Lake Malaren meets the Baltic Sea, and water is part of nearly every view. The medieval old town of Gamla Stan sits at its heart, with cobbled lanes, colourful buildings and the Royal Palace, while modern neighbourhoods such as Sodermalm and Ostermalm offer design shops, cafes and nightlife.

The museums are among Europe's best. The Vasa Museum houses a preserved 17th-century warship that sank on its maiden voyage, Skansen is the world's oldest open-air museum, and the ABBA Museum, the Nordic Museum and the Fotografiska photography museum draw crowds. City Hall, where the Nobel banquet is held, has a beautiful Golden Hall and tower views.

The city is clean, safe and easy to get around by metro, ferry and on foot. Summer brings long days and outdoor life, winter is dark and cosy with Christmas markets, and the archipelago offers island escapes all year. Plan three days to see the highlights.
